frame: world: the primary robot's base, REP-103 (x forward, y left, z up), metres; each check states its error's unit
limits: The suite checks the models against references for the cases it builds; it does not show that a model describes a real robot, lens or sensor. Monte Carlo checks are statistical: their tolerance is 4.5 standard errors of the estimated spread, at a fixed seed.

checks.title: Quaternion to rotation matrix
checks.quantity: largest element difference between DexVantage's rotation matrix and scipy's for the same quaternion
checks.reference: scipy.spatial.transform.Rotation.from_quat(...).as_matrix() (scalar-last, the same order DexVantage stores)
checks.note: Double precision rounding is about 1e-16 per element; 1e-12 leaves room for the products.

checks.title: Rotation matrix to quaternion
checks.quantity: largest angle between DexVantage's quaternion and scipy's for the same matrix, including half turns
checks.reference: scipy.spatial.transform.Rotation.from_matrix(...).as_quat()
checks.note: The angle of the relative rotation (scipy's magnitude, full precision near zero). The quaternion's sign is chosen with w ≥ 0, which the check also requires.

checks.title: URDF roll, pitch, yaw
checks.quantity: largest element difference between the rotation of an rpy triple and scipy's extrinsic x-y-z Euler rotation; and the round-trip angle error rpy → quaternion → rpy → quaternion
checks.reference: URDF's definition (roll about fixed x, then pitch about fixed y, then yaw about fixed z) as scipy from_euler('xyz', …), lowercase = extrinsic axes

checks.title: REP-103 optical frame
checks.quantity: largest difference between the optical frame's axes, expressed in the camera body frame, and REP-103's definition (z forward = body x, x right = body −y, y down = body −z)
checks.reference: REP-103 §"Suffix Frames", written out in the check
checks.note: Exact: the axes are a signed permutation, so any difference beyond rounding is a wrong axis.

checks.title: MuJoCo quaternion order
checks.quantity: largest element difference between DexVantage's rotation matrix and MuJoCo's mju_quat2Mat after the (x, y, z, w) → (w, x, y, z) conversion
checks.reference: MuJoCo's own C routine mju_quat2Mat (the library DexVantage exports to)

checks.title: Pose composition and inverse
checks.quantity: largest position difference (m) of points mapped through a chain of three poses and its inverse, against scipy rotations applied step by step
checks.reference: scipy Rotation.apply and vector addition, one link at a time

checks.title: IK round trip, 6-joint arm (full pose)
checks.quantity: largest tool position error of the IK solution, recomputed independently, over random reachable targets; every target must be solved and its rotation error be within 1 mrad
checks.reference: the target itself: the pose of a random collision-free joint vector, by a product of exponentials written out in the check (Rodrigues' formula; no MuJoCo), which also recomputes the solution's pose
checks.note: The tolerance is the solver's convergence tolerance (0.1 mm, 1 mrad): a solution reported as converged must meet it when its pose is computed by an independent route. The targets come from joint vectors inside the limits, so all are reachable and must be solved; MuJoCo's forward kinematics must also agree with the product of exponentials to 1e-12.

figure.title: Round-trip position error

checks.title: IK round trip, 5-joint arm (position only)
checks.quantity: largest tool position error of the position-only IK solution, recomputed independently, over random reachable targets; every target must be solved
checks.reference: the target position, from a product of exponentials written out in the check (no MuJoCo)
checks.note: A 5-joint arm cannot set all six pose coordinates; the solver reaches the position and gets the orientation as close as it can (as the target came from a real pose of the arm, the orientation is often reached too, which the detail counts).

checks.title: Manipulability of a planar 2R arm
checks.quantity: largest difference between √det(J Jᵀ) of the tip's planar (x, y) Jacobian and the closed form, over random joint angles including the stretched and folded singularities
checks.reference: the closed form w = |l₁ l₂ sin q₂| (Yoshikawa 1985), written out in the check
checks.note: MuJoCo's Jacobian is analytic, so agreement is to rounding (1e-12 m² for w of order 0.1 m²). The condition number is checked as well (relative error < 1e-6, away from the singularity, where it is infinite).

checks.title: Self-collision distance, two spheres
checks.quantity: largest difference between the signed distance of two spheres on non-adjacent links and the analytic one, over random placements (overlapping ones included); the in-collision flag must agree with the sign
checks.reference: the analytic distance |c₁ − c₂| − r₁ − r₂, written out in the check
checks.note: Sphere–sphere distance is closed form in MuJoCo as here, so agreement is to rounding.

checks.title: Self-collision distance, two capsules
checks.quantity: largest difference between the signed distance of two capsules on non-adjacent links and the analytic one, over random placements (overlapping ones included); the in-collision flag must agree with the sign
checks.reference: the closest points of the two axis segments (Ericson 2005, §5.1.9) written out in the check, minus the radii
checks.note: MuJoCo's capsule–capsule routine is a closed form as well (the closest points of the two axis segments), so agreement is to rounding; 1e-9 m, as for the spheres, flags any wrong branch of the segment-parameter clamping, which shows as millimetres.

checks.title: Forward kinematics: MuJoCo against product of exponentials

checks.title: Jacobian against finite differences
checks.quantity: largest element difference between the PoE chain's analytic Jacobian (twists moved by the adjoint) and central finite differences of its own forward kinematics, every link of the built-in robots
checks.reference: central differences, step 1e-6 rad or m, of PoEChain.fk; rotation by the log of R(q+h) R(q−h)ᵀ
checks.note: Central differences carry a truncation error of about h²/6 times the third derivative (1e-13 here) and a rounding error of about 1e-16/h = 1e-10; 1e-7 is well above both and well below any wrong column (of order the link lengths, 0.1 m).

checks.title: Jacobian: PoE against MuJoCo
checks.quantity: largest element difference between the PoE chain's world-frame Jacobian and MuJoCo's mj_jac (RobotModel.jacobian), at each link origin and at a random point fixed in each link, columns matched by joint name, every robot
checks.reference: MuJoCo mj_jac (another implementation of the same Jacobian)
checks.note: Both are exact formulas in double precision; 1e-9 allows for rounding only. The offset point (up to 0.2 m from the link origin on each axis) exercises the point argument and the link-to-world rotation that the origin alone does not.

checks.title: Robot-to-obstacle distance (project objects and surfaces)
checks.quantity: largest difference between env_distance (a sphere on a robot with a moved and rotated base, against a box, sphere, cylinder, convex mesh and table of the project) and the closed-form signed distance, over random joint positions, overlapping ones included; the nearest obstacle's name must match
checks.reference: the signed distance of a point to a box, sphere and cylinder, written out in the check, minus the sphere's radius
checks.note: MuJoCo measures sphere–box and sphere–sphere distances in closed form and sphere–cylinder and sphere–mesh through its convex solver (GJK, with EPA for penetration), whose convergence tolerance is far below a micrometre at these sizes; 1e-6 m is the solver's margin, while a wrong frame (the base pose, a quaternion order, a half-size taken for a full size) shows as centimetres.

checks.title: Coverage pixels per millimetre against OpenCV finite differences

checks.title: Pinhole and Brown-Conrady projection
checks.quantity: largest pixel difference between CameraModel.project and cv2.projectPoints for the same K and D (no distortion, five-term and eight-term rational Brown-Conrady), random points in front of the camera
checks.reference: OpenCV cv2.projectPoints (calib3d), an independent implementation of the same model

checks.title: Kannala-Brandt (fisheye) projection

checks.reference: OpenCV cv2.fisheye.projectPoints, an independent implementation of the same model

checks.title: Unprojection inverts projection
checks.quantity: largest pixel error of project(unproject(pixel)) over random pixels of the image, for every model (pinhole, Brown-Conrady, Kannala-Brandt, equidistant, equisolid, stereographic); the ray angle error of unproject(project(ray)) for random rays landing on the image must also be below 1e-9 rad

checks.note: The Brown-Conrady and Kannala-Brandt inverses are iterative (Newton, converged to 1e-12 in normalised units, about 1e-9 px); 1e-6 px allows for the image scale. Pixels with no ray (a Brown-Conrady model folding back before the corner) are counted, not compared.

checks.title: A model fitted to a stated FOV reproduces it
checks.quantity: largest difference between the field of view a CameraModel.from_fov model shows (fov_deg: edge to edge from its own unprojection) and the stated horizontal, vertical and diagonal angles, over every model and a range of image sizes and FOVs
checks.reference: the stated angles (for Kannala-Brandt, consistent H/V/D triples generated from pinhole, equisolid, equidistant and stereographic lenses written out in the check)
checks.note: The closed forms invert r(θ) exactly and the Kannala-Brandt fit passes through the stated points as constraints, so only rounding and the iterative inverse remain (about 1e-12°); 1e-6° is far below a datasheet's 0.1° rounding and catches an edge off by half a pixel (about 0.05° at 1000 px).

checks.title: Pixel density on a patch facing the camera
checks.quantity: largest relative difference between CameraModel.pixels_per_metre (closed form) and √|det J| of the 2 × 2 Jacobian of the projection of a small patch facing the camera, by central finite differences of project(); every model, points across the field, and tilted surfaces (normals)
checks.reference: finite differences of the projection itself (an independent derivative)
checks.note: Central differences with a step of 1e-5 of the range: truncation about 1e-10 relative, rounding about 1e-16 × 1000 px / 1e-5 ≈ 1e-8; 1e-6 leaves margin for both while any error in the closed form (a missing cos θ, the sin θ of the tangential direction) is 1e-2 or more away from the axis.

checks.title: Thin-lens depth of field
checks.quantity: largest relative difference between depth_of_field (solved from the blur-disc equation) and the near and far limits from the hyperfocal distance H = f²/(N c) + f: near = s (H − f)/(H + s − 2f), far = s (H − f)/(H − s) (infinite from s ≥ H)
checks.reference: the hyperfocal-distance formulae of photographic optics, written out again in the check
checks.note: Two algebraic forms of the same thin-lens result; only rounding separates them (about 1e-15 relative). 1e-10 catches any slip in either.

checks.title: Thin-lens defocus blur disc
checks.quantity: largest relative difference between blur_circle_px and the blur disc from the thin-lens equation 1/f = 1/z + 1/v written out here (image distances v_s, v_z; disc A |v_z − v_s| / v_z on the sensor at v_s, A = f/N); and the blur at the depth-of-field limits must equal the circle of confusion
checks.reference: the Gaussian thin-lens equation and similar triangles, written out again in the check and evaluated in exact rational arithmetic
checks.note: The reference is computed in exact rational arithmetic (fractions.Fraction) from the same floating-point inputs, so the error is DexVantage's own rounding: a few 1e-16, amplified by s / |s − z| because the focus distance passes through a metre-to-millimetre conversion. Points within 0.1 % of the focus distance are moved to 0.1 % from it, bounding that to about 1e-13; 1e-11 leaves margin.

checks.title: Pinhole camera against MuJoCo-rendered fiducial masks
checks.quantity: largest distance between the centroid of a sphere's MuJoCo segmentation mask and the centroid of the mask CameraModel predicts (pixel centres whose ray passes within the sphere's angular radius); three MuJoCo cameras (fovy; focal + sensorsize; focalpixel + principalpixel), 63 spheres each
checks.reference: MuJoCo's OpenGL renderer (mujoco.Renderer, EGL, segmentation, no multi-sampling) on a scripted MJCF scene
checks.note: Both masks sample the same pixel centres, so they differ only where MuJoCo's drawn sphere (a 128 × 64 polygon mesh, inscribed in the sphere) or its rasteriser's edge rule decides a boundary pixel the other way. One such pixel moves the centroid of a 150–200 px mask by about (its distance from the centroid) / (mask area) ≈ 7 / 180 ≈ 0.04 px; 0.1 px allows two. A focal length 0.1 % off, or a principal point 0.1 px off, would show as more at the image edge (0.3 px for 0.1 % at 320 px from the centre). Every mask must be found and overlap its prediction by at least 95 % (intersection over union).

checks.title: Pinhole projection of sphere centres against MuJoCo renders
checks.quantity: largest distance between the centroid of a sphere's MuJoCo segmentation mask and the centre of its image predicted by CameraModel.project (midway between the projections of the two tangent rays in the plane of the optical axis, which removes the perspective bias); same scene as optics.mujoco_fiducial_masks
checks.reference: MuJoCo's OpenGL renderer (mujoco.Renderer, EGL, segmentation, no multi-sampling) on a scripted MJCF scene
checks.note: The centroid of a mask sampled at pixel centres is not the centre of the ellipse it samples: for these 14 px fiducials the sampling error alone, measured on CameraModel's own predicted masks against the predicted centres, is reported as sampling_error_max_px (about 0.2 px). 0.3 px is that measured sampling error with the 0.1 px of the mask check added. Comparing with the projected sphere centre without the ellipse correction would add the perspective bias (perspective_bias_max_px), which grows with the angle from the axis and the sphere's size.

checks.title: Camera view pixel distances against exact ray casting
checks.quantity: fraction of sampled pixels (away from silhouettes) whose distance in the Camera view image differs from the exact first hit along the same lens ray by more than 1 mm, or where only one finds a surface; UR5e sample, every imager, a Brown and a fisheye lens, random arm poses
checks.reference: core/raycast.py first_hit (Möller–Trumbore through a uniform grid) along CameraModel.unproject rays
checks.note: Both measure the distance to the same triangle's plane along the same lens ray, so away from silhouettes they agree to rounding. Near a silhouette the image answers for its pixel centre (pinhole) or for the nearest pixel of its base or cube image, so a ray grazing an edge may land on the other side: those are counted but not held against it (they must stay under 3 % of the pixels). Hits closer than 1 cm, where the two near-clip rules differ, are left out.

checks.title: Coverage shares against projection and exact ray casting
checks.quantity: largest absolute difference of the task-volume shares (seen by ≥ 1 camera, by ≥ 2, and by each camera) between the coverage study and an independent path; scripted scene with a box, a cylinder, a table and three static cameras
checks.reference: pinhole projection written out from the stated FOV and core/raycast.visible_exact (Möller–Trumbore through a uniform grid), with the voxels inside the objects found by a test written out again

Half a percent of the volume leaves room for those voxels and nothing else. Per voxel, the disagreement must stay under 2 %, the occlusion answers farther than two texels from a silhouette must agree but for 1e-3 (rounding at the near clip), and the in-image answers but for 1e-4 (a voxel centre exactly on an image edge).

checks.note: The cube map answers per texel (2/n rad at a face centre), so a point within about a texel of a silhouette may be judged by a ray that passes the edge on the other side; those are counted but not held against it (they must stay under 2 % of the points). checks.title: Cube-map visibility on both samples against exact ray casting
checks.quantity: fraction of random task-volume points whose cube-map visibility differs from exact ray casting, pooled over the SO-100 and UR5e samples, every camera, three arm poses and every cube-map backend available
checks.reference: core/raycast.visible_exact: Möller–Trumbore ray–triangle intersection through a uniform grid, sharing no code with either rasteriser; the tolerance is the measured share of points within half a texel diagonal of a silhouette
checks.note: The cube map answers per texel: a point is judged by the ray through its texel's centre, at most half a texel diagonal from its own line of sight (√2/n rad = 0.16° at a face centre for n = 512; less towards a face's edges). So a point can be judged wrongly only when an occluder's silhouette passes within that angle of it, and the tolerance is the share of points that close to a silhouette, measured on these scenes with raycast.near_silhouette (a subsample of 1,000 points per map; half_texel_band_fraction). Disagreements farther than a whole texel (2/n rad) from any silhouette are faults: at most 1e-3 of the points may be there.
